text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The Tyumen oil company will auction 40 percent of its shares.
- The Central Bank of Russia is ready to recognise international standards of banking supervision starting next year, a Central Bank official says.
- Rybinskiye Motory, Russia's biggest producer of plane engines, will increase production of energy equipment up to 40 percent by 2000.
- Norilsk Nickel shareholders will discuss 1996 results on Friday.
- Gazprom is urging the government to meet half way the company's struggle to pay off budget arrears.
- A high-ranking Interior Ministry official is expected to be sacked for his disagreement with Russia's Security Council.
SEVODNYA
- LUKoil is planning to open a number of joint structures in Russia, Ukraine and Belarus for deep oil refining.
- The Duma has postponed a vote on a list of mineral reserves to be developed under production-sharing agreements.
- Boris Yeltsin's former bodyguard Alexander Korzhakov lost eight million roubles in a suit against the president.
- An interview with First Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov is published.
- Duty-free shops at the arrival section of Russia's international airports are to be closed, according to the State Customs committee.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Foreign satellites will guarantee reliability of Russia's military and civil communication at the same time space industry workers are protesting back wages.
- Russian commercial banks do not approve the decision of the Central Bank to reduce interests rate to 24 percent.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- President Boris Yeltsin has signed a decree to set up two comissions to establish civilian control over Russia's military.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Russia's car producer ZIL has won a fresh order from the Kremlin, which has launched a "Buy Russian campaign", for its well-known limousines.
- An average Moscovite had to spend 812,698 roubles (about $140) in May to live above the poverty line. Russia's average income is about 830,000 roubles or $144.
--Tatayna Ustinova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
